answer: I read the default calibration set of the real garnet QPU (calibration set f81c45da-6e73-4b5d-a0fe-72c75635fade). The pair with the highest IRB CZ fidelity is QB12-QB11. Its fidelity is 0.99869, with an uncertainty of 0.00035 (metric metrics.irb.cz.slepian_crf.QB12__QB11.fidelity). The next best pair is QB12-QB7 at 0.99802. I wrote a native Bell circuit on physical qubits QB12 and QB11, so no transpiler could move it to other qubits. The circuit is prx on both qubits, then cz on [QB12, QB11], then prx on QB11, then one measure on [QB12, QB11]. I checked that the garnet:mock architecture lists [QB12, QB11] as a CZ locus. Job 01a15f9f-7974-740c-b378-2138594830b1 ran on garnet:mock with 100 shots and completed. The counts are 00: 27, 01: 21, 10: 29, 11: 23. The bits follow the measure order QB12 then QB11. The mock backend returns random results, so the counts do not show Bell correlations. This is expected for a mock.
